patterns: Price before education: 13 of 14 priced sales calls had zero beats before the first number. The exceptions were Fleming (2) and Kicinski (1), and Sweetlove got 3 but no price. Typical: "Is your property under an acre?" -> "Okay. All right. So we have two options... One is a quick fix."

Quick Fix first, every time: 14 of 14 priced calls led with QF and none led with TMCP plus a recommendation. He called TMCP 'best' or 'most successful' only after QF on 5 calls (Fleming, Shawan, Rasmussen, Johnson, Lucas). TMCP closed on 3 (Quaschnik, Lucas, and Fleming's open quote). Kern got 'Do you want both of them?' and both quotes are still unapproved.

Capture is strong: 10 of 15 sales calls had full capture with the address read back verbatim, e.g. "Let me confirm that it's 10510, 33rd Street, East Edgewood, 98372." Every promised quote was sent within about 10 minutes under Muhammad's name. Data gaps remain: Fleming's phone was mistyped, and Quaschnik's veteran discount never reached the quote.

The guarantee was said on 12 of 14 priced calls ("if we don't catch anything, then we wouldn't charge you anything other than the setup fee"). Missed on Kern and Candy Ford. The $150-credit bridge ("your 150 deposit will be count as a month and a half paid") came up on 6 calls, but each time as an argument to start with QF.

Out of area and service callers get invented or vague answers: 5 D grades of 17 service calls. Examples: "We are working on it and pretty soon we'll be able to" (Everett, Lynnwood), turning away Key Peninsula before the zip, and the made-up 'bi weekly' TMCP cadence (Horvath, Sexton).
